(a) the best results are obtained by using a combination of local hill climbing, integer linear programming, and entity clustering, (b) the best local optimization method is based on hill climbing, (c) the best entity clustering algorithm is based on the Louvain method, and (d) the best results were obtained by combining all of these techniques.

Collective disambiguation of spots in Web text as references to entities from a Wikipedia catalog can be formulated as a global optimization problem, and practical solutions can significantly outperform recently developed local algorithms.

(1) the collective annotation of entity references on Web pages is feasible and useful, and (2) the best collective annotation algorithm is a greedy algorithm that uses pre clustering of Wikipedia entities to reduce the search space and then performs a hill climbing search over the remaining space, using an objective function that combines the local compatibility and a global coherence measure.
